identification: Victorian/Edwardian style oval hinged locket (about 20x25mm) on a rose-toned belcher chain with a barrel clasp. Front: radiating starburst engraving either side of a vertical engraved band; back: different engraved foliate pattern (photo 2 shows both faces). Catalogued 9ct; no hallmark visible. Style typical of c1890-1915 lockets, many of which are 'back and front' (gold sheet over base metal) rather than solid, so the 9ct claim matters.

viewing_check: Look with a loupe for 9ct/375 or Birmingham/Chester hallmarks on the locket bezel, bail and the barrel clasp; any 'B&F' (back and front) mark means gold-cased, low value. Check worn high spots of the engraving for base metal showing through. Weigh locket and chain separately. Check the hinge, catch and inside (photos or hair add a little).
